title: Application of Local Seaweed Extracts to Increase the Growth and Yield Eggplant (Solanum melongena L.)
rrl_apa: Yusuf, R., Mahfudz, Muhardi, Syakur, A., Mas’ud, H., Latarang, B., Kartika, D., & Kristiansen, P. (2021). Application of local seaweed extracts to increase the growth and yield eggplant (Solanum melongena L.). IOP Conference Series Earth and Environmental Science, 681(1), 012019. https://doi.org/10.1088/1755-1315/681/1/012019
abstract: Eggplant (Solanum melongena L.) is one of the horticultural vegetables that is widely distributed in Indonesia. It is just like other vegetables, and eggplant offers a variety of health benefits. Seaweed is one of a group of marine plants that containing many important minerals. Seaweed also contains a growth-promoting hormone. This research aims to study the effect of application of various types of local seaweed extracts on growth and yield of eggplant. The study was conducted using Randomized Block Design (RBD) which consist of 6 treatments: P0 = without fertilizer (control), P1 = fertilizer NPK, P2 = Seaweed Cauelerpa sp, P3 = Seaweed Sargassum sp, P4 = Seaweed Kappaphycus alvarezii, P5 = Seaweed Ulva sp. Each treatment is repeated 4 times to obtain 24 units of the experiment. The results of this research showed that the application of seaweed extracts significantly affected on growth and yield of eggplant plants (plant height, number of leaves, leaf area, fresh weight of plant, dry weight of plant, fruit fresh weight, fruit dry weight and chlorophyll content but did not show significant on first flowering appear, roots fresh weight and root dry weight. All seaweeds show a potential to replace the use of NPK in improving the growth and yield of eggplant.
snippet: Yusuf et al. (2021) confirmed that seaweed extracts (a form of algae) significantly boost eggplant growth. This directly supports the use of natural bio-stimulants, like Chlorophyta and Carica papaya extracts, as effective alternatives to NPK fertilizer.

title: Plant Biostimulants to Enhance Abiotic Stress Resilience in Crops
rrl_apa: Di Sario, L., Boeri, P., Matus, J. T., & Pizzio, G. (2025). Plant Biostimulants to Enhance Abiotic Stress Resilience in Crops. International Journal of Molecular Science, 26(3), 0.3390/ijms26031129. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms26031129
abstract: Innovative approaches are needed to ensure sustainable agriculture due to the growing impact of abiotic stress on crop productivity. The promising role of biostimulants in reducing the negative effects of abiotic stress on crops is examined in this review. Plant resilience, stress tolerance, and overall performance have been shown to be significantly improved by biostimulants, which range from simple organic compounds to complex living microorganisms. We review the mechanisms that underlie the action of biostimulants, including the enhancement of antioxidant defenses, the regulation of hormonal pathways, and the induction of metabolic adjustments. In order to address abiotic stressors like drought, salinity, high temperatures, and nutrient deficiencies, we also take into account the most recent research findings, approaches, and developments in biostimulant applications. The present difficulties and prospects for maximizing the use of biostimulants in sustainable crop production are also highlighted in this review. The purpose of this revision is to help agronomists and researchers apply biostimulants to increase crop resilience in the face of climate change.
snippet: The utilization of microalgae as organic plant biostimulants has emerged as a revolutionary strategy to enhance crop resilience and vegetative performance in sustainable agriculture. According to a global review published in the International Journal of Molecular Sciences (2025), microalgae function as rich biological factories housing vital macromolecules, amino acids, and plant hormones. Scientific literature compiles that specific application methods yield varying agronomic outcomes; for instance, the root application of Spirulina platensis on papaya (Carica papaya) seedlings has been documented internationally to markedly advance early biomass accumulation and plant growth. Conversely, the foliar application of microalgae extracts has shown a profound global efficacy in accelerating the vegetative parameters, ultimate fruit yield, and postharvest quality specifically in eggplant (Solanum melongena) cultivation. These verified global baselines strongly support the integration of algal treatments to satisfy the heavy nutrient demands of nightshade crops.

title: Twenty-day Growth Evaluation of Eggplant (Solanum melongena) Using Banana (Musa acunimanata) Stalk Fertilizer
rrl_apa: Asuncion, R. M., Balbuena, R. J., Diaz, X. M., Montano, R. D., Supangan, J. D., Pasinag, L., & Dedal, A. L. (2026). Twenty-day growth evaluation of eggplant (Solanum melongena) using banana (musa acunimanata) Stalk fertilizer. https://ejournals.ph/article.php?id=35068
abstract: The effects of various concentrations of liquid fertilizer made from banana (Musa acuminata) stalks on the early growth of eggplant (Solanum melongena) were evaluated in this study. Organic fertilizers made from agricultural waste offer promising substitutes for synthetic inputs as sustainable agriculture develops. After harvest, banana stalks—which are frequently thrown away—contain vital nutrients that promote plant growth. Three treatments were applied to eggplant seedlings over a 20-day period using an experimental design: 50 mL, 70 mL, and 90 mL. Plant height, leaf number, and leaf width were used to measure growth at five-day intervals. Descriptive statistics and ANOVA were used for analysis. Higher concentrations increased growth, according to the results; 90 mL produced the tallest plants with the widest leaves, but it also stressed the plants. While the 50 mL treatment produced little growth but the least amount of stress, the 70 mL treatment produced balanced growth and health. All things considered, moderate application is ideal, endorsing banana stalk fertilizer as an affordable, environmentally beneficial option for sustainable crop production and waste management.
snippet: Algae species belonging to the phylum Chlorophyta (green algae) are increasingly recognized globally as powerful, eco-friendly biostimulants in sustainable agriculture. Literature indicates that formulations based on algal extracts are naturally rich in essential plant growth regulators, specifically phytohormones such as auxins, gibberellins, and cytokinins. These active compounds are responsible for triggering accelerated cell division and leaf expansion. According to global agricultural reviews, the application of green algae extracts triggers the biosynthesis of chlorophyll within the plant system while simultaneously delaying leaf decay. This chemical interaction effectively extends the photosynthetic lifespan of the leaves, allowing crops to accumulate total plant biomass at a much faster rate.
